Reason: The ultrasound images demonstrate multiple variable-sized cystic lesions in the fetal lung (indicated by arrows), and the color Doppler image confirms the absence of significant internal blood flow within the mass. These findings are characteristic of Congenital Cystic Adenomatoid Malformation (CCAM) Type II, which typically has a better prognosis than Type I or III and is often managed conservally with postnatal monitoring unless hydrops or severe compression develops.
